sections.overview: The catalogue uses Scinax agilis; Amphibian Species of the World currently treats it as Ololygon agilis.
sections.identification: The field paper gives no diagnostic description in its abstract.
sections.habitat: It inhabits coastal restinga in four Brazilian states.
sections.diet: No species-specific diet is given in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Bromeliads were the most-used microhabitat in one Bahia study.
sections.reproduction: The current ASW account notes that the larva remains undescribed.
sections.ecology: The study links it to flooded coastal plains and their plant communities.
sections.conservation: The study flags local loss of restinga vegetation as a concern.
